assign.request: Port three more MIT, vanilla-or-reimplementable Codrops demos (a reveal/transition named in the paging vocabulary, a scroll-driven layout, a text effect); add to the hub's DEMOS and children; prove with ui-test at four widths and reduced-motion.
assign.now: scoping — read round-2.md, requirements.md, round-1 readme, paging mechanisms vocabulary
steps: read briefs + round 1 rules + paging mechanism vocabulary
shortlist + license-check candidate repos (github MIT search)
read source of 3 chosen repos, decide substitutions
wire into codrops hub (DEMOS + children + table)

log.msg: Licence pass (same method as round 1: api.github.com/search/repositories?q=org:codrops+license:mit, then the actual LICENSE file, never the badge). Read LICENSE for 5 shortlisted repos - UnrevealEffects, StickySections, TypeShuffleAnimation, SlicedTextEffect, TextRepetitionEffect - all genuine MIT (Codrops 2009-2021/22), READMEs clean (no redistribution caveat).

Picked: UnrevealEffects (page transitions via covering elements + clip-path - the circle variant, index2.html) for the reveal/transition slot; StickySections (15 sticky-section-exit demos, demo1+demo3 combo: dim+scale+translate as the next section covers it) for scroll-driven layout; TypeShuffleAnimation (character-scramble text effect, fx1/fx3/fx6) for the text effect. All three ship GSAP (+ ScrollTrigger/Lenis on StickySections, +Splitting.js on TypeShuffle) despite MIT licence - same round-1 answer: reimplement the mechanism in plain CSS/JS, note the drop in the table.

Rejected: SlicedTextEffect and TextRepetitionEffect (both GSAP+ScrollTrigger+Lenis scroll-text effects - too close to the sticky-stack slot, one scroll demo is enough this round). KineticTypePageTransition, CoverPageTransition, PixelTransition (all page-transition candidates, MIT, not checked further - UnrevealEffects fit the reveal wording exactest and is the simplest to reimplement without a dependency). ScrollBasedLayoutAnimations, TileScroll, ElasticGridScroll, ScrollPanels (scroll candidates, not checked further once StickySections fit).

assign.now: built all 3, wired into hub, ui-tested

log.msg: Bug found+fixed via ui-test: sticky-stack's initial scroll-progress read ran before View.stylesheet()'s async <link> applied the stage's real height, baking progress=1.000 into every panel's inline style instead of 0 (measured via a debug Playwright script, ai/2026-09-05/codrops-2/). Fixed with a ResizeObserver on the stage that re-runs the same update once real layout lands - re-verified correct (0.026 to 0.645 to 1.000 as the demo is scrolled).

ui-test: drive.mjs plans at 400/1280/1920/3440 for all 3 (scratchpad/codrops-2/*-plan.json + *-out/steps.json); doc.sw===doc.cw at every step on all 3 - zero real horizontal overflow (drive.mjs's own offscreen-x flag false-positived on every post-viewport-resize step, the same known stale-vp.width-closure bug round 1 hit - cross-checked, not a real bug). Zero console errors once still.png existed (3 404s each beforehand, expected per round 1's own finding). Gestures proven: circle-reveal click-to-open+back at all 4 widths, sticky-stack real scroll (scrollBy on its own container) with --progress read back at each step, type-shuffle all 3 buttons with frame-by-frame text capture proving genuine mid-scramble state (not just before/after). Separate script (Playwright reducedMotion:'reduce' context, drive.mjs has no media-emulation verb) proved: circle-reveal's transition-duration collapses to 0s and opens instantly, sticky-stack's JS never touches --progress (stays at its CSS default), type-shuffle's click jumps straight to the settled phrase with the trigger button never disabling - all PASS.

assign.outcome: **Codrops round 2 lands: three more MIT demos, all wired into the hub.** [`/imagine/codrops/`](/imagine/codrops/) now shows 6 cards + a 6-row table. New: [Circle reveal](/imagine/codrops/circle-reveal/) — ported from `UnrevealEffects` (MIT), the click-to-cover transition drawn as a **fifth visual of this realm's own `swap` mechanism** (same stage, no url change), not a new mechanism name. [Sticky stack](/imagine/codrops/sticky-stack/) — ported from `StickySections` (MIT), a bounded scroll stage (`overflow-y:auto`, its own `scroll` listener) where each panel dims/scales as the next covers it. [Type shuffle](/imagine/codrops/type-shuffle/) — ported from `TypeShuffleAnimation` (MIT), 3 of its 6 character-scramble effects, no Splitting.js. All three drop the original's GSAP/Splitting.js/Lenis for plain CSS/JS, documented per-demo in the table. Real bug found+fixed via ui-test: sticky-stack's first progress read ran before its own (async) stylesheet applied, baking a wrong value into every panel — fixed with a `ResizeObserver` that re-runs the read once real layout lands. `ui-test` (drive.mjs, 4 widths each) + a separate Playwright script (`reducedMotion:'reduce'` context, since drive.mjs has no media-emulation verb) both green: zero real horizontal overflow (drive.mjs's own `offscreen-x` flag false-positived on the stale-viewport bug round 1 also hit — cross-checked via `scrollWidth===clientWidth`), zero console errors once stills existed, every reduced-motion path verified PASS (transition collapses to 0s / JS never starts / click jumps straight to settled text). Rejected: SlicedTextEffect + TextRepetitionEffect (too close to the sticky-stack slot), KineticTypePageTransition/CoverPageTransition/PixelTransition (UnrevealEffects fit "reveal" exactest, simplest to reimplement). Private server (port 8121, killed on landing) — never touched port 80.
